pages.title: Imaginary Unit
pages.text: A number whose square is minus one, which sounds like nonsense until you notice that it simply rotates the number line by a right angle. A tachyon's mass is imaginary, and this tiny bead was distilled from exactly that. It looks perfectly ordinary until you turn it, when it seems to point somewhere sideways.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A tachyon's rest mass squared is negative, so its mass itself must be an imaginary number. I condensed tachyon flux over a tachyon crystal and pinned the result against the real continuum, and the leftover factor was i.
